newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police arrest men over grenades - paper.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police arrest men over grenades - paper.

text.p: Police have arrested two Indonesians for possessing two hand grenades police believed were to be exploded during a Moslem mass gathering last week, newspapers reported on Saturday.

The Jakarta Post quoted chief of the city police investigation department Colonel Paimin Aboeamar as saying on Friday the two men, Abdul Aziz Umar Mahdie and Saleh Abdullah, were arrested with the grenades on February 9 at their respective homes.
During a raid in Saleh's house, a foreigner was also arrested for questioning, said Aboeamar without giving other details.
The Eid al-Fitr celebration which was said to be the men's intended target took place in Monas square in central Jakarta on February 9 and 10.
President Suharto and other high-ranking officials had attended a gathering on the evening of February 8 at the Monas square to mark the end of the Ramadan fasting month.

Aboeamar said police raided the suspects' houses after receiving information the two men planned to take the South Korean-made explosives to the gathering. He said the grenades were powerful enough to destroy at least one floor of a multi-story building.

The Media Indonesia newspaper quoted Aboeamar as saying police believed the suspects planned to detonate the grenades. He said police intentionally kept the finding a secret in order not to create unrest during the celebration.
The paper gave no other details.
